headline: The ten-year closed at 5.24%. Nothing else mattered.
standfirst: Monday belonged to the bond market again: the ten-year rose 7.6bp to 5.236%, its highest close since 2007, the thirty-year touched 5.58% and the two-year 4.93%, and the S&P 500 fell 0.77% to 7,683.69 — its lowest in ten sessions — with the Dow down 0.67% to 51,481.51 and the Nasdaq 0.92% to 26,820.38. Oil did the pushing, Brent trading near $108 in the afternoon after Trump's weekend rejection of Iran's Hormuz offer, before an Axios report of a US sanctions-relief offer knocked it back and lifted stocks off their lows; Trump then called the report fake. Gold fell 3% to a seven-week low. Overnight the RBA hiked to 4.60% and said more may be needed, the Nikkei fell 1.4% and the Kospi 1.3%, and the dollar sits near a two-month high. Tuesday is JOLTS, consumer confidence, six Fed speakers and, if Qatar's mediators are right, Washington's reply to Tehran.

bullets.title: Rates: 5.24% on the ten-year, 4.93% on the two-year, and a Fed still talking it higher
bullets.text: The ten-year closed at 5.2361%, up 7.56bp, after touching 5.24% — the highest since 2007 and within 9bp of that year's 5.3228% peak; the thirty-year reached 5.581% intraday, a high not seen since the early 2000s, and closed near 5.57%; the two-year rose 7.89bp to 4.9305%, its highest since 2023, so every maturity from three years out now yields above 5% and the two-year is a session away. The long Treasury ETF fell 0.88% and is down 12.28% over twelve months. Governor Cook said inflation pressures will persist for several months and that AI productivity gains will not arrive fast enough this year to offset them, noting data-centre demand has pushed electricity and water costs up about 5%; Barkin said supply shocks are no longer temporary and laid out two paths without saying which needs more tightening; Bowman spoke only on supervision. Trackers put October at 68–72.5% and at least one more hike by December at about 94%, with roughly 91bp priced over the next year. UBS pointed out the Fed has not hiked at an October meeting before an election since 1990 and expects the pricing to migrate to December and beyond; Commerzbank has December as the last hike. Treasury's stepped-up buybacks of long bonds have not capped the move.

bullets.title: Equities: a ten-session low, Meta and Tesla down 4–5%, Nvidia up on a $150 billion buyback
bullets.text: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 both closed at their lowest in ten sessions; the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.08%, the Russell 2000 0.69%, and the VIX rose 8.07% to 16.07. At the lows the Dow was off more than 400 points and the S&P 500 about 1%; the bounce came at midday on the Axios sanctions report and faded when it was denied. Meta fell 4.79%, Tesla 3.94%, Amazon 1.41%, Microsoft 1.35% and Apple 0.78%; Nvidia rose 1.68% after adding $150 billion to its buyback and on reports Beijing may let Alibaba and ByteDance buy its latest chips, and the Golden Dragon China index rose 1.12%. Energy, up 0.10%, staples and health care were the only sectors to close higher; communication services lost 1.58%, consumer discretionary 1.41% and financials 1.19%. Europe was flat — DAX −0.13%, CAC +0.01%, FTSE −0.10% — while Shanghai fell 1.67% to a seven-week low and the ChiNext 4.53%, and India's Nifty lost 1.54% to close below 23,000 for the first time since April, with the Sensex at its lowest close since March and foreign investors net sellers of about ₹5,350 crore. This morning: Nikkei −1.36%, Kospi −1.25%, Hang Seng −0.96%, ASX −0.16%, Shanghai flat, Nifty −0.37%. OpenAI's developer day and Trump's AI meeting with technology chief executives are both today.

bullets.title: Oil and Iran: a reply due through Qatar, exports at 80% of normal, and a Brent roll to read correctly
bullets.text: Trump said in the Oval Office on Monday that US officials had spoken separately with mediators, gave no detail, and said the US would win "pretty quickly" and that petrol prices would fall when it did; the afternoon announcement was a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa, alongside a rollback of fuel-economy standards. Araghchi met Qatari mediators in New York and said he expects Washington's response "hopefully by Tuesday" before returning to Tehran; Iran's plan gives the US four to five days to release frozen funds, lift oil sanctions and end the port blockade, with nuclear talks starting within seven. Trump denied the Axios report that he had offered sanctions relief — "I offered them NOTHING" — and repeated over the weekend that strikes could resume after November's midterms. On the physical side, Kpler has Middle East crude exports back to just under 80% of pre-war levels, the highest since February, with Hormuz clearance at 10.6 million barrels a day on Saturday against a 17.1 million baseline, and Saudi Arabia's east–west pipeline running about 3.5 million barrels a day, half its capacity; the IEA still has the fourth quarter in a 2.2 million barrel a day deficit. Prices: Brent reached about $108 on Monday afternoon and WTI $95 before both eased; this morning November Brent is $105.91, up 0.6%, and WTI $93.32, up 0.8%. The November Brent contract expires on Wednesday and December trades about $6 lower — near $98–100 — which is why the market map's Brent row prints −4.76% today. It is a roll, not a sell-off. OPEC+'s monthly meeting of seven producers is this week.

bullets.title: The RBA hiked to 4.60% and left the door open; the dollar, the yen and gold
bullets.text: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised the cash rate 25bp to 4.60% in a unanimous decision — the fourth hike of 2026, a full percentage point this year, and the highest since November 2011. The statement said some of the upside risks flagged in August are materialising, with further disruptions to global oil supply, fuel prices partly passed into other goods and services, and growth and inflation both higher than expected; the board judged further tightening warranted and said it will do what is necessary, including raising rates again. Core inflation is 3.6% against a 2–3% band; markets price another hike by February and an each-way bet on a third in 2027. AUD/USD barely moved at $0.702 and the ASX 200 was flat; Wednesday's August CPI, seen 4.0% after 3.5%, matters more than the press conference. The dollar index is 101.2, near a two-month high and up about 1.8% in September, its best month since June. The euro is $1.1367, a three-month low, after Lagarde told the European Parliament the ECB will take measured steps; sterling is $1.3248. USD/JPY is 157.35 after Japan's top currency diplomat Mimura said markets should heed last week's "very clear" joint warning and Katayama said she and Bessent agreed to strengthen cooperation; the market treats 160 as the line. Gold fell 3% on Monday to $4,156, its lowest since 5 August and down about 7% in September; spot is $4,124 this morning, silver $60.62, platinum $1,700.

bullets.title: Today and the week: JOLTS, six Fed speakers, then PCE, ISM and an 84,000 payrolls consensus
bullets.text: Tuesday: Lagarde again at 07:00 ET; FHFA house prices at 09:00; JOLTS at 10:00, seen 7.23 million after 7.27 million — openings have missed for two months — alongside Conference Board confidence seen 89.0 after 89.4, a third straight fall; then Bowman at 11:00 on supervision, Barr on the economic outlook at 12:40, Goolsbee 13:00, Musalem 13:30, Williams 14:00 and Waller on payments at 15:00, with BoE's Mann and Tenreyro in between. Carnival reports. Tuesday evening at 21:30 ET: Australia's August CPI seen 4.0% and China's PMIs, NBS manufacturing seen 50.1. Wednesday is quarter-end: ADP seen 72,000 after 38,000; core PCE seen +0.3% on the month and 3.4% on the year after 0.2% and 3.3%, headline 3.7% unchanged with the monthly +0.4%; final Q2 GDP 1.5%; Chicago PMI 51.0 after 47.1; German HICP seen 3.2% after 2.9%; UK final GDP; Micron after the close; Cook 15:25 ET, Goolsbee 16:05, Kashkari 18:00; the Tankan at 19:50 seen 25. Thursday: Swiss CPI seen 1.0%; ISM manufacturing seen 54.9 after 54.6 with prices paid 72.5; claims 200,000; Waller, Jefferson, Bowman, Cook and Williams; Lagarde a third time; Nike after the close; Tokyo CPI; Chinese markets shut for Golden Week. Friday: euro-area HICP seen 3.6% after 3.2% with core 2.5%; payrolls, where consensus has drifted to about 84,000 from 100,000 a week ago, after 162,000, with Barclays at 50,000; unemployment seen 4.1%, earnings +0.3%. Then Williams on 6 October, the FOMC minutes and ten-year auction on the 7th, the thirty-year and the ECB accounts on the 8th, the banks on the 13th, and CPI with the Beige Book on the 14th.

calendar.note: Second appearance in two days. Monday's "measured steps" took the euro to a three-month low; Friday's HICP is seen 3.6%.
Openings seen 7.23 million after 7.27 million; confidence seen 89.0 after 89.4. Soft prints are the only thing this week that trims October before PCE does or does not.

calendar.event: Fed's Barr on the outlook; Goolsbee 13:00, Musalem 13:30, Williams 14:00, Waller 15:00
calendar.note: Six Fed voices in four hours, with Bowman at 11:00 on supervision. Barr called for more hikes last Wednesday; Williams is on his fourth appearance in a week.
Seen 4.0% after 3.5%, the morning after the RBA hiked to 4.60% and said more may be needed. NBS manufacturing seen 50.1 after 49.8.

calendar.event: PCE (August); final Q2 GDP; ADP 08:15; quarter-end
calendar.note: Core PCE seen 0.3% on the month and 3.4% on the year after 3.3%; headline 3.7%. The print the Fed named, on the day rebalancing flows are largest. November Brent expires today.

calendar.event: Micron Q4 after the close; Kashkari 18:00
calendar.note: Earnings seen about $31 a share against $3 a year ago, with options implying a 9% move. Kashkari is the last Fed speaker of quarter-end day, after the PCE print.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing (September); Nike after the close
calendar.note: Seen 54.9 after 54.6 with prices paid 72.5 after 71.1. The flash PMI said 57.0; a matching ISM confirms the repricing. China shuts for Golden Week.

Consensus has slipped to about 84,000 after 162,000, unemployment 4.1%, earnings +0.3%. With October near 70%, a strong print removes the last doubt; a weak one is the only thing on the calendar that could take the hike away.

sessionNote: Tuesday opens with the ten-year at 5.24% and the two-year 8bp from 5%, S&P futures soft after Monday's ten-session low, Brent near $106 for the November contract, gold at a seven-week low and the dollar near a two-month high. The session has two data points at 10:00 ET and six Fed speakers from 11:00 to 15:00, with Barr at 12:40 the one who has already said "more". The headline risk is Iran: Araghchi expects Washington's answer through Qatar by Tuesday, and Monday showed the reaction function — a report of concessions took Brent $3 off its high and stocks off their lows within the hour, and a denial took half of it back. Two things to have straight before the open: the November Brent contract expires tomorrow and December is $6 lower, so any oil quote you see this week needs a contract attached; and tomorrow is quarter-end with PCE at 08:30, so today is the last day to position before the flows. In trading terms, the ten-year's 5.2361% close is the level — equities have not rallied with it above 5.20% — and the two-year at 5% is the next headline the bond market will write.
watchOut: Trading an oil chart without knowing which contract is on it. November Brent expires on Wednesday; December trades about $6 below it; the source table behind our market map has already switched and prints Brent −4.76% on a day the physical barrel is up. From Thursday every continuous-front-month chart will show a gap that no barrel actually traded through, and WTI produced the same illusion last week. If a level on your chart sits inside that gap, it is not a level. The second trap is Monday's: an unsourced report of US concessions was worth $3 on Brent and 60 S&P points for about two hours, and was called fake by the President before the close. With Washington's reply to Tehran due through Qatar today, expect more of the same, and size for the reversal, not the headline.

archive.headline: Trump said no. Oil is back above $107.
archive.summary: Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz offer over the weekend and Brent recovered Friday's fall before New York opened; gold fell to its lowest since early August, the Kospi lost 2.5% and the dollar hit a two-month high. The front end eased with October's hike odds while the long end kept rising, into a week of PCE, ISM and payrolls.

archive.headline: The week the Treasury market stopped waiting for the Fed
archive.summary: Weekend edition. The ten-year went from 4.95% to 5.21% in a week on a 58.4 flash PMI, three auctions at two-decade highs and eight Fed speakers, and every Treasury from two years out cleared 5%. Equities held on Meta and AMD while the Dow fell for a fourth week, Brent round-tripped $100–$99–$106 on Iran, and October was 71% priced for a second hike.

archive.headline: A survey took the ten-year to 5.11%. An auction kept it there.
archive.summary: A flash composite PMI of 58.4, the highest since July 2021, took the ten-year up 14.6bp to 5.116% — its worst day since April 2025 — and a $70 billion five-year auction stopped at 5.033%, the highest since 2006. Barr said further hikes were likely needed and October went to 73% priced; every sector but energy fell and Brent rose back above $100.

archive.headline: The Fed said “we’ll see”. The two-year auction said 4.787%.
archive.summary: Treasury sold $69 billion of two-years at 4.787%, the highest stop since May 2024, on demand that held; Brent settled at $99.25 for its first close under $100 since 9 September; four Fed officials, none voting this year, all leaned toward more. The Nasdaq closed at a second straight record while financials fell 1.97%.

archive.headline: An App Store ranking moved a trillion dollars
archive.summary: Meta's Muse agent topped the US iPhone chart and the CPU complex repriced around it: Meta +11.43%, AMD +9.95% to a first $1 trillion close, Intel +12%, Arm +17%, and the Nasdaq to its first record since June. Crude fell to an eleven-day low on Hormuz shipping data and the ten-year came back under 5%, into a $69 billion two-year auction.

archive.headline: The war premium leaks out before the UN
archive.summary: Monday with no US data and a live diplomatic wire. Crude fell for a fourth session as traders priced a chance of US–Iran contact at the UN General Assembly and Saudi Arabia worked to restore its East–West pipeline, with the ten-year coming into the day at 5.01% after its first close above 5% since July 2007.

archive.headline: The hike landed. The bond market blinked first.
archive.summary: Weekend edition. The Fed's unanimous 25bp on Wednesday took the Dow down 631 points and Thursday gave most of it back, with the S&P up 1.14% to 7,637.76 as the ten-year fell to 4.93% and oil slid. The weekend risk was the Iran war, with Trump saying he was near a decision on resuming large-scale strikes.
